title: B2 BUILD (control-plane): precedent.py displacement-bridge enforcement on the overrule path, plus tests
description: Enact AB5 and section A.3.1 in code: publishing with --overrules requires embedding the overruled record's ratio VERBATIM together with its authorship (record id, published_by, issuing task) inside the superseding record; refusal otherwise. PR-009 is the worked precedent being generalized - it preserved the defeated counterargument inside the superseding record; the DIRECTIVE turns that courtesy into a protocol. The point is jurisprudential, not cosmetic: the superseding record becomes a citation that keeps paying its predecessor, which is what makes proper overruling cost the overruled author nothing. Implement EXACTLY the enforcement spec in docs/precedent-research/synthesis-addendum-ii-spec.md, citing its requirement id on each enforcement branch. Runs in parallel with T-371, which owns disjoint files.
acceptance_criteria: OWNS: .harness/bin/precedent.py (sole writer in this epic) and ONE new test file .harness/tests/test_precedent_bridge.py. You MAY amend assertions in test_precedent.py, test_precedent_v2.py or test_precedent_conflicts.py ONLY where your own change invalidates them, and you must list every amended assertion in the handoff with its reason. You MUST NOT touch .harness/tests/test_precedent_seed.py (its assertions run against the live registry and it is owned by nobody in this epic), MUST NOT touch .harness/bin/reputation.py or .harness/tests/test_reputation.py (T-371 owns both and runs concurrently), and MUST NOT touch PRECEDENT.md (T-372's file).

IMPLEMENT EXACTLY WHAT THE SPEC FIXES, verbatim, with the requirement id in a comment on each enforcement branch. Invent nothing. If the spec is underdetermined at the keyboard, implement its stated default and record an OPEN-QUESTION note; do not silently choose. If it has no stated default for a case you hit, hand off blocked naming the case.

THE ENFORCEMENT: `publish --overrules` REFUSES with exit 1 and a named message unless the overruled record's ratio is embedded VERBATIM together with all three authorship elements - record id, published_by, and issuing task. The refusal message names which element is missing. The shipped exit-code contract is unchanged: 1 REFUSAL, 2 usage, 3 FINDINGS, 4 registry integrity.

THE DECISION-ANCHOR CASE, per the spec's explicit ruling: a decision:T-NNN#anchor target has no published_by and no registry ratio, and PR-009's own live target decision:T-344#R-2 is exactly that shape. Implement the ruled behavior and test it as its own case.

PYTHON 3.9.6, STDLIB ONLY, no 3.10+ syntax anywhere (no match statement, no dataclass slots). Reuse harness_common (guarded, atomic_write_json, append_jsonl, now_iso, agent_id) rather than reimplementing any of it, and change NO harness_common signature. Route any event through the module-local emit_event so an overridden root never writes to the live log (V1-06/V1-48, the measured contamination defect).

TESTS: at least 6 new tests in test_precedent_bridge.py, each as its own test method - refusal with no embedded ratio; refusal with the ratio but each of the three authorship elements missing in turn; success with the complete embedding, asserting the stored field content matches the predecessor's ratio byte-for-byte; the decision-anchor case; and the NEGATIVE CONTROL, that a publish with no --overrules is completely unaffected (the enforcement must not tax ordinary publishes). Every test runs under an overridden root: zero writes to .harness/precedents/ and zero new lines in .harness/logs/events.jsonl.
